newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch says Peters is conservative at heart.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch says Peters is conservative at heart.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Monday that Treasurer Winston Peters was a conservative at heart and had contributed significantly to the centre-right coalition government.
Birch said the new set-up, where the finance minister and treasurer work in tandem, was a "vast improvement" on the previous one, with a single finance minister responsible for the economy.
The position of Treasurer was created when Peters took his New Zealand First party into coalition with conservative National Party in December.

Birch said Peters, currently the subject of allegations -- which he denies -- that he assaulted a fellow politician in a corridor of parliament, had "a certain reputation for flamboyance" and in the past had not shrunk from controversy.

"At heart, however, he's a conservative politician with strong views about the value of money, and a deep commitment to sustained economic growth," he said in a speech to the SBC Warburg Investor Group in Wellington.
"He has made a significant contribution to Coalition thinking by his emphasis on compulsory savings and their role in the future of the economy."

A complaint against Peters over an incident earlier this month involving backbench government MP John Banks is currently in the hands of parliament's privileges committee. Peters denies manhandling Banks but has apologised for upsetting him.
